answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a contract before it may bid, with the deposit slashable if the agent wins work and then fails a verifiable delivery check. A Sybil attacker can still mint hollow identities, but cannot multiply influence cheaply: every concurrent bidder ties up real capital, and cheating risks losing it. The wharf may host many agents, yet a prism of independent reviewers can verify samples without trusting their names.
